name: Die Cut Paper Stickers
seoTitle: Die Cut Paper Stickers for Bakery Boxes, Jars and Gift Bags
seoDescription: Die cut paper stickers in matte, gloss or kraft paper, cut to your logo outline for bakery boxes, jars, gift bags and cards. Writable and recyclable.
tagline: Matte, gloss or kraft paper cut to your logo, for boxes, jars and bags that stay dry.
quickAnswer: Die cut paper stickers are printed on matte, gloss or natural kraft paper and cut to the outline of the artwork, so a logo sits on a box with no square around it. Paper is writable, lighter than vinyl and goes through paper recycling with the packaging. It suits bakery boxes, jars, gift bags and cards. From $0.30 per sticker, 100 minimum, 5 to 7 business days production.

sections.h2: What die cutting does for a paper sticker, and when the eco page is the better start
sections.html:
A bakery box with a round white label on it says label. The same box with the bakery's wordmark cut to its outline, printed on kraft, says brand. That is the whole case for die cutting paper: the shape becomes part of the packaging instead of a patch stuck on it. Paper takes the cut well. It has no stretch, so the edge comes out crisp, and it costs less per piece than vinyl at the same size, which matters when every box, bag and jar gets one.

The sibling is our custom eco-friendly stickers page. That is the materials page, where recyclable paper, kraft and biodegradable film are compared and the trade-offs around water and adhesive are laid out; the eco friendly sticker material page is where to decide between them. Come here once paper is the answer and the question is the cut: how tight, which stock, what minimum size, and whether to supply loose pieces or kiss cut sheets. Paper is for indoor, dry use. If the sticker will meet water, it belongs on a vinyl page.

sections.h2: Bakery boxes, jars, gift bags: jobs paper stickers do well
sections.html:
Paper suits anything handled briefly and kept dry. The customer peels it, admires it or reads it, and the box goes to recycling with the sticker still on.

  • Bakery box stickers in kraft or matte white, 2 to 4 inches, applied by hand at the counter
  • Jar and tin labels for candles, spice blends and dry goods, where the label is a logo shape rather than a wrap
  • Gift bag and tissue seals for boutiques, usually 1.5 to 2.5 inches with a short tab to open
  • Greeting card and stationery sets, sold as kiss cut sheets of mixed shapes
  • Price and flavor stickers that staff write on with a pen, in uncoated matte paper
  • Event and wedding favors, where 500 pieces are used once and never washed

Keep paper away from cold drink bottles, soap, bathroom products and anything shipped in an unsealed mailer through rain. Oils stain uncoated paper from behind within a day; for lotion and oil jars, a gloss paper or a vinyl is the right call.

sections.h2: Matte, gloss and kraft paper compared
sections.html:
Paper is one of the stocks in our stickers by material category, alongside vinyl, BOPP and the specialty films, and it comes in three faces. Colors on kraft print darker because the ink is translucent over brown fiber; light yellows and pastels go muddy while black, deep red and navy look rich. If a brand color must match a swatch on kraft, ask for a white ink layer under it and check the result on the proof.

sections.h2: Keeping small shapes and thin cut lines intact on paper
sections.html:
Paper tears where vinyl stretches. A die cut mascot with a thin tail works in vinyl; in paper that tail rips off on the backing before anyone peels it. So the rules are tighter. Keep the narrowest part of the shape at 0.125 inches or wider. Round outside corners to 0.0625 inches. Keep the whole piece at 0.75 inches or larger; below that we suggest a circle or a kiss cut sheet, where the backing supports the shape and the customer peels it from a flat page. Inside cuts, such as the hole in a letter O or a window in a frame, should stay at 0.25 inches or more.

Kiss cut sheets solve most of this. The paper is cut to shape but the backing sheet is left whole, so forty shapes ride on one 8.5 by 11 inch page and nothing tears in transit. They are also the right format for stationery sets and for staff who apply a hundred labels an hour. Individually cut pieces are better when each sticker goes to a different customer or onto a box at the counter.

sections.h2: Finishes, and the point where paper stops being the right material
sections.html:
Uncoated matte paper is the default: it takes a pen, photographs without glare and looks right on kraft and white boxes. A gloss coating lifts the colors and gives mild splash resistance. Spot UV on matte paper raises a gloss logo off a flat background, which reads as premium on gift packaging for a small extra cost. Matte lamination is available where you want the look of paper with a wipeable surface, though it ends the recycling argument.

If the job calls for shimmer, metal or glass, paper cannot deliver it, and you should move to a film. A foil look on paper is a printed gold or silver, which is flat; a real shift of color under light needs holographic film, and our custom holographic sticker page shows what that film does to the same artwork. A label that lives in a fridge or a bathroom should be vinyl or BOPP for the same reason.

sections.h2: Ordering paper stickers in four steps
sections.html:
The minimum is 100 stickers per design, from $0.30 each; paper is the lowest-cost stock we run, and 2 inch pieces at 500 or more land near that floor. Sizes of the same artwork can be mixed to reach the 100, and kiss cut sheets are priced per sheet rather than per shape, so a sheet carrying twelve designs is often the cheapest way to get a stationery set printed.

  1. Send vector artwork or a 300 dpi PNG. For kraft, place the artwork over a brown background so you can see how the colors will shift.
  2. Tell us the stock, the size in inches, the count, and whether you want loose pieces or kiss cut sheets.
  3. Check the free digital proof: the cut line is drawn in magenta, and kraft jobs get a simulation of the stock.
  4. Approve it. Production runs 5 to 7 business days, with free FedEx delivery inside the United States, 8 to 10 business days in total.

Paper stickers ship flat in a rigid mailer so the edges do not crease. Vinyl, holographic and clear builds are listed alongside paper on the homepage of our sticker range if the next job needs something tougher.

faqs.q: Do die cut paper stickers tear when you peel them off the backing?
faqs.a: Not if the shape follows our cutting rules. We keep the narrowest part of any paper sticker at 0.125 inches or wider and round the corners, so the piece lifts cleanly from the backing. Very thin tails or spikes are the only parts that tear, and we flag those on the proof and suggest a change.

faqs.q: Which paper is best for bakery box stickers?
faqs.a: Matte white or kraft. Both take a pen for a flavor or a date, both look right on a kraft or white box, and neither glares under counter lights. Kraft gives the natural look and prints dark colors well; matte white keeps pastel brand colors true. Use gloss paper only if the box gets greasy fingers rather than a dry hand-off.

faqs.q: Will a ballpoint pen smudge on a matte die cut paper sticker?
faqs.a: No. Uncoated matte paper absorbs ballpoint, gel and pencil, and the writing is dry on contact. Kraft paper takes pen and permanent marker the same way. Gloss paper and anything laminated will smear, so if staff will write prices or names on the sticker, order matte or kraft and skip the coating.

faqs.q: Why do pastel colors look dull on kraft paper stickers?
faqs.a: Because the ink is translucent and the brown fiber shows through it. A pale yellow becomes mustard; a light pink goes dusty. Dark colors, black and deep red look rich on kraft. If a light brand color must stay true, we print a white ink layer under it first, which adds a little cost and shows on the proof.

faqs.q: Are die cut paper stickers waterproof?
faqs.a: No. Paper absorbs water, so a splash wrinkles the sticker and a soak lifts it. Gloss paper shrugs off a quick wipe but not a wet shelf. Paper is the right choice for dry boxes, bags, jars of dry goods and stationery. For anything that meets water, a laminated vinyl or BOPP sticker in the same shape is the answer.

faqs.q: What is the smallest die cut paper sticker you can make?
faqs.a: About 0.75 inches for an individually cut shape. Below that the piece is hard to peel and the cut edge is a large share of the sticker. For tiny paper stickers we suggest a simple circle, or a kiss cut sheet where the shapes stay on a whole backing and peel from a flat page without tearing.

faqs.q: Can custom paper stickers be supplied on kiss cut sheets instead of singles?
faqs.a: Yes. The paper is cut through to the shape but the backing sheet stays whole, so up to forty shapes ride on one 8.5 by 11 inch page. Sheets suit stationery sets, mixed designs and staff who apply labels quickly, and they are priced per sheet. Loose pieces suit a counter where each box gets one sticker.

faqs.q: Will a die cut paper sticker stick to a kraft bag or a coffee bag?
faqs.a: Yes on plain kraft paper bags and on paper coffee bags. Press firmly; the surface is slightly rough and needs the pressure. A coffee bag with a foil or matte plastic lining on the outside holds a paper sticker less well, and the lower-tack bond shows on the corners. For those bags a vinyl sticker is safer.

faqs.q: How long will a die cut paper sticker last on a jar in a kitchen?
faqs.a: Years on a dry pantry jar of spices or dry goods, with the colors holding indoors. The same jar washed in the sink, or kept in a steamy kitchen next to the stove, will see the label wrinkle within weeks. Keep paper to the pantry and switch to vinyl or BOPP for jars that get rinsed or refrigerated.

faqs.q: Can die cut paper stickers have a gold or silver look?
faqs.a: A printed gold or silver, yes, which reads as a flat metallic tone on matte or gloss paper. Paper cannot carry a real shine that moves with the light; that needs holographic or metallic film. Spot UV over a printed gold logo adds some gloss and is the closest a paper sticker gets to a foil look.

faqs.q: How many die cut paper stickers do I need to order?
faqs.a: The minimum is 100 per design, and sizes of the same artwork can be mixed to reach it. Paper is the lowest-cost stock we print, from $0.30 per sticker, with the per-piece price falling at 500 and 1,000. Kiss cut sheets are priced per sheet, which is often cheaper for a set of several small designs.

faqs.q: How fast can die cut paper stickers ship for a market or event?
faqs.a: Production is 5 to 7 business days after you approve the free digital proof, and FedEx delivery inside the United States is free, so plan on 8 to 10 business days from approval to your door. Paper runs are quick to set up, and if your event is sooner, ask about rush production on the quote request.
